title: Add a library of named queries stored as files
description: Adds `jmespath/library.py` so our tools can share saved queries instead of pasting expressions around. `QueryLibrary(root)` keeps each expression as a text file: the name `users/active` is the file `users/active.jmespath` under `root`. `save(name, expression)` checks that the expression parses, then writes it atomically, replacing any earlier query of that name; a save that fails leaves the saved query as it was. `get(name)` returns the compiled expression and caches it until the file changes on disk, so hand edits are picked up, and `search(name, data)` runs it. In a file, lines whose first non-blank character is `#` are comments, and the expression may span several lines. `names()` lists every query, sorted. A root that does not exist yet is an empty library: opening or reading a library never writes to disk, and the first save creates the root. `delete(name)` removes the file and any directories that become empty, but never the root. Names come from users, so a name that resolves to a file outside the root raises `InvalidQueryNameError`, and an unknown name raises `UnknownQueryError`. Includes tests.

defects.summary: The containment check is a string prefix test, so a name like ../queries-private/secret reaches a sibling directory whose name starts with the root's name.
save writes the file before checking that the expression parses, so a failed save replaces a working query with a broken one.
delete prunes empty directories with os.removedirs, which keeps climbing past the root and removes the root and its empty parents.
defects.corrected:
directory = os.path.dirname(path)
        while directory != self.root and not os.listdir(directory):
            os.rmdir(directory)
            directory = os.path.dirname(directory)

defects.summary: Comments are cut at the first # anywhere on a line, so a # inside a string literal truncates the expression.
defects.corrected:
lines = [line for line in f.read().splitlines()
                 if not line.lstrip().startswith('#')]

defects.summary: The constructor creates the root directory, so merely opening or listing a library that does not exist yet creates it (and fails where the directory cannot be created).

ceiling.summary: names() deletes dot-prefixed .tmp files, which are the temporary files _write is still filling for a save in progress, so listing a library writes to disk and makes a concurrent save fail at os.replace.

decoys.why: A root that does not exist yet is documented as an empty library; save creates it.
The broad except only removes the temporary file and re-raises, so nothing is swallowed.
